a2-01.q: Fill in the blanks: El sábado Ana ___ tarde a la estación y después ___ por el andén.
a2-01.why: Ana is 'she': -ar verbs take -ó (llegó) and -er verbs take -ió (corrió). Llegió and corró mix up the two endings; llegué and corrí are the 'I' forms.

a2-01.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Ana saw a message and said "What luck!"'?
options: Ana vió un mensaje y dijo: «¡Qué suerte!».
Ana vio un mensaje y dició: «¡Qué suerte!».
Ana vio un mensaje y dijo: «¡Qué suerte!».
Ana veyó un mensaje y dijo: «¡Qué suerte!».
a2-01.why: Ver gives vio, with no written accent (like dio and fue). Decir has the irregular stem dij- and ends in plain -o: dijo, not dició. Veyó doesn't exist.

a2-01.topic: Ir a + infinitive, and ir a + place
a2-01.q: What does 'Voy a llegar primero' mean, compared with 'Voy a Valencia'?
options: Both are future plans with a verb after 'a'.
Both mean that I already went somewhere.
The first is a destination; the second is a future plan.
The first is a future plan (I'm going to arrive first); the second is a destination (I'm going to Valencia).
a2-01.why: After a, an infinitive (llegar) signals a near-future plan, while a place (Valencia) tells you where you are going.

a2-01.q: Pablo says he bought two bus tickets yesterday. Fill in the blank: Ayer ___ dos billetes de autobús.
a2-01.why: For yo, -ar verbs end in -é with a written accent: compré. Compró is he/she, -í is the yo ending for -er/-ir verbs, and compre without the accent is not the preterite.

a2-01.q: Which sentence has a mistake in the preterite?
options: Ana y Pablo llegaron a Valencia.
a2-01.why: Subir is an -ir verb, so the 'they' form ends in -ieron: subieron. The -aron ending is only for -ar verbs (llegaron).

a2-01.q: Fill in the blank: Los padres de Ana ___ que el tren tenía una avería.
a2-01.why: After the j of the stem dij-, the 'they' ending is -eron, not -ieron: dijeron. Decir never uses a regular stem in the preterite, so decieron is wrong.

a2-01.topic: Ir a + infinitive, and ir a + place
a2-01.q: Fill in the blank: Mañana yo ___ tocar la guitarra en la boda.
a2-01.why: The near future is ir + a + infinitive: voy a tocar. 'Voy tocar' drops the a, va a is the wrong person, and al (a + el) only goes before a masculine noun: voy al pueblo.

a2-01.topic: Ir a + infinitive, and ir a + place
a2-01.q: Fill in the blank: Ana y Pablo van ___ pueblo.
a2-01.why: A destination takes ir a + place, and a + el always becomes al: van al pueblo. 'A el' is never written, pueblo is masculine (not a la), and ir uses a, not en, for where you are going.

a2-02.q: The note in the box tells Sofía to go to the market. Which tú command completes it? 'Primero, ___ al mercado.'
a2-02.why: Ir has an irregular tú command: ve. Va and vas are present-tense statements ('goes', 'you go'), and ves comes from ver ('you see').

a2-02.topic: Object pronouns: le dio, te lo regala
a2-02.q: In 'Ella te lo regala', what does lo stand for, and why does te come first?
options: Lo is the thing given (the puppy); te is the person receiving, and the indirect pronoun always goes first.
Lo means 'to him', so it should really go before te.
Lo is the person receiving; te is the thing given.
Lo is the puppy, but the order is free, so 'lo te regala' is also correct.
a2-02.why: With two pronouns, the indirect one (to whom: te) goes first and the direct one (what: lo = el cachorro) second: te lo = it to you. 'Lo te' is never correct.

a2-02.q: Put the story events in order: 'Entonces, el perro saltó a sus brazos. Primero, Sofía abrió la caja. Después, corrió por la calle.'
options: Después, corrió por la calle. Primero, abrió la caja. Entonces, el perro saltó.
Primero, el perro saltó. Entonces, abrió la caja. Después, corrió.
Primero, Sofía abrió la caja. Después, corrió por la calle. Entonces, el perro saltó.
Entonces, el perro saltó. Después, corrió. Primero, abrió la caja.
a2-02.why: Primero starts the sequence, después (afterwards) continues it, and entonces (then, at that moment) introduces what happened next.

a2-02.topic: Object pronouns: le dio, te lo regala
a2-02.q: In 'El panadero tomó los mangos y le dio un pan dulce', who receives the sweet bread?
a2-02.why: Le is the indirect object pronoun: it shows who receives (to her). In the story the baker gives the sweet bread to Sofía; le never refers to the subject (the baker).

a2-02.q: Turn the statement into a tú command for Sofía: 'Sofía lleva los mangos a la panadería' > '___ los mangos a la panadería, Sofía.'
a2-02.why: For regular verbs, the tú command looks like the he/she present: lleva. Llevas is a statement ('you take'), lleve is the formal usted command, and llevar is the infinitive.

a2-02.topic: Object pronouns: le dio, te lo regala
a2-02.q: Fill in the blank: Doña Fabiola ___ dio una bolsa de mangos (a Sofía).
a2-02.why: Sofía receives the bag, so she is the indirect object: le = to her. La would make Sofía the thing given, and se is not used alone here.

a2-02.q: Fill in the blank: El abuelo llegó a las nueve ___ mañana.
a2-02.why: After a clock time, Spanish uses de la mañana (at nine in the morning). Without a clock time it's por la mañana: Por la mañana, el abuelo llegó.

a2-02.q: What is the tú command of venir (to come)?
a2-02.why: Venir has a short irregular tú command: ven (like ve, pon, sal). Vienes and viene are statements, and venga is the formal usted command.

a2-03.topic: Irregular preterite: fue, puso, hice, dijo
a2-03.q: Fill in the blank: Abuela, ayer yo ___ tu receta.
a2-03.why: Hacer has the irregular stem hic-, and the yo form ends in -e with no accent: hice. Hizo is he/she (c becomes z); hací and hicé don't exist.

a2-03.q: Mateo tastes the dish (el plato) he has just cooked. How does he say 'It tastes good'?
a2-03.why: Estar describes how food tastes as you experience it: está rico. Es rico would describe a general quality (and with a person, ser rico means 'to be rich'). Hay means 'there is'.

a2-03.topic: Irregular preterite: fue, puso, hice, dijo
a2-03.q: Fill in the blank: —___ que tomar el autobús de las seis —dijo la abuela.
a2-03.why: Tener has the irregular preterite stem tuv-, and the yo form ends in -e with no accent: tuve. Tuvo is he/she; tení and tuvé don't exist.

a2-03.q: Mateo's mother tastes the dish and says '¡Me encanta!'. What does she mean?
a2-03.why: Encantar works like gustar: the dish is the subject and me shows who loves it. Me encanta = I love it (lit. it delights me).

a2-03.topic: Irregular preterite: fue, puso, hice, dijo
options: Mateo puso aceite en la sartén.
a2-03.why: Irregular preterites never take a written accent: hizo, puso, dijo, fue. 'Hizó' is wrong.

a2-03.q: Fill in the blanks: —¿Dónde ___ la receta? —En el cuaderno. ___ una receta muy vieja.
a2-03.why: Location uses estar (¿Dónde está?), and saying what something is (identity) uses ser: Es una receta muy vieja.

a2-03.q: Fill in the blank: Para la receta, ___ dos ingredientes.
a2-03.why: Faltar works like gustar: the missing things are the subject, so the verb agrees with them. Dos ingredientes is plural, so faltan; falta is for one thing (falta algo).

a2-03.q: Fill in the blank: A Mateo le ___ los tomates.
a2-03.why: With encantar the verb agrees with the thing that is loved. Los tomates is plural, so encantan; le shows the person (to Mateo).

a2-04.q: Which sentence describes a childhood habit?
options: Todos los días jugaba al fútbol en la calle.
Ayer jugó al fútbol en la calle.
Jugué una vez al fútbol en la calle.
Va a jugar al fútbol en la calle.
a2-04.why: The imperfect (jugaba) with todos los días describes a regular habit in the past. Jugó and jugué are single events, and va a jugar is the future.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blank: Faltaban dos minutos cuando el árbitro ___ un penalti.
a2-04.why: The referee's whistle is the event that interrupts the background (faltaban dos minutos), so it takes the preterite: pitó.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blank: Todos ___ a los dos hermanos.
a2-04.why: People take conocer, with a before the person: conocían a los dos hermanos. Saber is for facts, and todos is plural, so the singular forms conocía and sabía don't fit.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blanks: Tomás ___ adónde va a tirar Natalia porque ___ muy bien a su hermana.
a2-04.why: Where she will kick is a fact, so saber: sabe adónde. Knowing a person is conocer: conoce a su hermana.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blank: Cuando Tomás ___ pequeño, vivía en Medellín.
a2-04.why: Describing a stage of life (cuando era pequeño) is background, so it takes the imperfect of ser: era. Fue and estuvo present it as a finished event, and es is present.

a2-04.q: Natalia asks Tomás: '¿Cómo lo supiste?' What does she mean?
options: How did you use to know it?
How did you find out (know) it?
a2-04.why: Supiste is the irregular preterite of saber (stem sup-). In the preterite, saber means 'found out' or 'knew' at that moment.

a2-04.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Tomás was very nervous, but he remembered something'?
options: Tomás estuvo muy nervioso, pero recordaba algo.
Tomás fue muy nervioso, pero recordó algo.
Tomás estaba muy nervioso, pero recordó algo.
Tomás está muy nervioso, pero recordó algo.
a2-04.why: His nervousness is the background (imperfect of estar: estaba), and remembering is the event (preterite: recordó). Ser is not used for a temporary feeling.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blank: Cuando eran pequeños, Natalia siempre ___ el balón a la izquierda.
a2-04.why: Siempre and cuando eran pequeños describe a past habit, so the imperfect: tiraba. Tiró is a single event, tira is present and va a tirar is future.

a2-05.q: Which sentence sets the scene (weather and time) at the start of a story?
options: Llovió mucho y fue de noche.
Va a llover y es de noche.
Llovía mucho y era de noche.
a2-05.why: Weather and time of day are background, so the imperfect is used: llovía, era. Llovió and fue present them as completed events.

a2-05.q: How do you say 'I was working' (at that moment)?
a2-05.why: Imperfect of estar + gerund (-ando) describes an action in progress at a past moment. Trabajado is the participle.

a2-05.q: Lisandro writes to a stranger. Which is the most polite way to ask for help?
a2-05.why: The conditional softens a request: ¿Me podría ayudar? = Could you help me? The other options are orders or demands.

a2-05.q: What does '¿Te gustaría cenar con nosotros?' mean?
options: Did you like having dinner with us?
Would you like to have dinner with us?
Do you have to have dinner with us?
a2-05.why: Gustaría is the conditional of gustar: ¿Te gustaría...? = Would you like...? It is a polite invitation, not a past event (gustó) or an obligation (tener que).

a2-05.q: Fill in the blank: Ella vivía en el número 7, y en la calle ___ un chico con una mochila roja.
a2-05.why: Había (the past of hay) introduces what existed in the scene: 'there was'. It stays singular even with plural nouns, era can't mean 'there was', and hay is present.

a2-05.q: What does 'La mamá de Lisandro bajó corriendo' mean?
options: Lisandro's mother used to run downstairs every day.
Lisandro's mother got out of the car and stopped running.
Lisandro's mother got out of the car in a hurry (running).
Lisandro's mother is going to run.
a2-05.why: A gerund after a movement verb says how the action was done: bajó corriendo = she got out running, in a hurry. Bajó is one preterite event, not a habit.

a2-05.q: Fill in the blank: ___ pedir unas empanadas. (We could order some empanadas.)
a2-05.why: The conditional of poder uses the short stem podr- + -íamos: podríamos = we could. Podemos is 'we can', pudimos is preterite, and poderíamos doesn't exist.

a2-05.q: Fill in the blank: Ahora estoy ___ solo en la calle.
a2-05.why: Estar + gerund (-ando) describes an action in progress right now: estoy esperando. Esperado is the participle, and espero/esperar can't follow estoy.

a2-06.q: How do you say 'Try it' (la bombilla) as a tú command?
a2-06.why: An affirmative command attaches the pronoun to the end, and a written accent keeps the stress on prue-: pruébala. La prueba means 'she tries it' (or 'the test').

a2-06.topic: Por vs para: por la tarde, para ti
a2-06.q: Don Rafael gives Camila a bulb. Fill in the blank: Es ___ ti.
a2-06.why: Para marks the person who receives something: es para ti = it's for you. Por ti would mean 'because of you'.

a2-06.topic: Por vs para: por la tarde, para ti
a2-06.why: Parts of the day take por: por la mañana, por la tarde, por la noche.

a2-06.q: What does 'Esta lámpara te dará luz' mean?
options: This lamp will give you light.
This lamp is giving you light.
This lamp gives you no light.
a2-06.why: Dará is the simple future of dar (dar + á): it will give. Te comes before the verb.
Di is the irregular tú command of decir; me (to me) and lo (it) attach to the end, indirect first: dímelo. 'Give it to me' would be dámelo.

a2-06.topic: Por vs para: por la tarde, para ti
a2-06.q: In 'Vamos a subir todo por la escalera', what does por show?
options: the way they move: up the stairs
a2-06.why: Por is used for movement through or along a place: por la escalera = up/by the stairs.

a2-06.q: Fill in the blank (I will be): Aquí ___ feliz.
a2-06.why: The future adds -é to the whole infinitive: ser > seré. Soy is present and era is imperfect.

a2-06.q: Which sentence is a plan with ir a + infinitive, not the simple future?
options: Voy a comprar una ahora mismo.
a2-06.why: Voy a comprar is ir a + infinitive, the usual way to talk about a plan. Dará, estaré and seré are simple future forms.

a2-07.q: Fill in the blank: Todas las tardes Rodrigo tocaba la guitarra, pero un jueves se ___ una cuerda.
a2-07.why: The routine is imperfect (tocaba), and the one-time event on a Thursday is preterite: se rompió.

a2-07.q: Rodrigo showed the guitar to Ernesto. Which is correct, replacing 'la guitarra' with a pronoun?
a2-07.why: Le becomes se before lo/la, the indirect pronoun comes first, and la is feminine to match la guitarra.

a2-07.q: Fill in the blank: Es muy bonita, pero es más vieja que ___.
a2-07.why: After que in a comparison, use the subject pronoun: más vieja que yo (older than me / than I am). Mí is only used after prepositions such as para (para mí).

a2-07.q: Rodrigo says to Ernesto: 'Quiero pagártelo.' What do te and lo mean?
options: te = the shop, lo = the money
te = Ernesto (to you), lo = it (the new string)
a2-07.why: Pronouns can attach to an infinitive, indirect first: pagar + te (to you, Ernesto) + lo (it, the string): I want to pay you for it.

a2-07.q: Which time phrase goes with the imperfect in this story?
a2-07.why: Todas las tardes describes a routine, so it goes with the imperfect (tocaba). The others point to one moment and go with the preterite.

a2-07.q: In 'Ernesto le cambió la cuerda', who or what is le?
options: Rodrigo: Ernesto changed the string for him
a2-07.why: Le is an indirect pronoun: the person who benefits (for him = Rodrigo). The string is the direct object, la cuerda.

a2-07.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Julieta is his best student'?
options: Julieta es mejor alumna que él.
Julieta es su más buena alumna.
Julieta es su alumna más mejor.
a2-07.why: Bueno has the irregular form mejor; with a possessive it means 'best': su mejor alumna. 'Más buena' and 'más mejor' are wrong here.

a2-07.q: Fill in the blank: Julieta nunca hablaba, pero siempre ___ un poquito.
a2-07.why: Siempre and the habit in the sentence (nunca hablaba) call for the imperfect: bailaba.

a2-08.q: How do you say 'They didn't see anybody'?
a2-08.why: When nadie comes after the verb, no goes before the verb: no vieron a nadie. The a is needed because nadie is a person they see.

a2-08.topic: Obligation: hay que, tener que, deber
a2-08.q: What does 'Si hay niebla, hay que caminar despacio' mean?
options: If there is fog, there is a slow path.
If there is fog, you can't walk.
If there is fog, he walked slowly.
If there is fog, you have to walk slowly.
a2-08.why: Hay que + infinitive is a general obligation: one has to / you have to walk slowly.

a2-08.q: The woman says to Valeria and Andrés: '___ son los turistas.' Which word fits?
a2-08.why: Two people, so plural 'you'. In Colombia that is ustedes, with the they-form son. Vosotros (sois) is only used in Spain.

a2-08.topic: Obligation: hay que, tener que, deber
a2-08.q: Fill in the blank (we): ¿Qué ___ que hacer?
a2-08.why: Tener que is for a specific person and changes: nosotros tenemos que. Deber does not take que, and hay que does not take a person.

a2-08.q: Fill in the blank: Andrés dice: «No veo ___».
a2-08.why: Nada = nothing (things); nadie = nobody (people). With no before the verb, Spanish uses nada, not algo.

a2-08.q: Why is there no 'no' in 'Nadie respondió'?
options: Because it is in the preterite.
Because nadie comes before the verb.
It's a mistake; it should be 'Nadie no respondió'.
a2-08.why: When the negative word starts the sentence, it is enough on its own: Nadie respondió. After the verb you need no: No respondió nadie.

a2-08.q: In 'Jairo los está buscando', who are los?
a2-08.why: The woman is talking to Valeria and Andrés, so los means 'you all': Jairo is looking for you.

a2-08.topic: Obligation: hay que, tener que, deber
a2-08.q: Which sentence correctly says 'You must follow the river' to one friend?
a2-08.why: Deber + infinitive, with no que and no a: debes seguir. Hay que is followed by an infinitive, not a conjugated verb.

a2-09.q: How do you say 'I have never been late'?
a2-09.why: Present perfect = he + participle (-ado for -ar verbs): he llegado. Nunca goes before he, and nothing goes between he and the participle. Llegando is the gerund.

options: She is going to get dressed quickly.
a2-09.why: Vestirse (reflexive) means to get dressed: the se refers back to Daniela. Dressing someone else would be vistió a alguien, se vio would be 'saw herself', and se vistió is preterite, not future.

a2-09.q: Mrs. Ortega says to Daniela in the interview: 'Llega tarde.' What does the verb form show?
options: It is a command to arrive.
Usted is used (formal), with the he/she verb form.
Tú is used (informal); llega is the tú form.
a2-09.why: Formal usted takes the he/she verb form (llega, tiene). With tú it would be llegas, tienes. Mrs. Ortega uses usted with Daniela throughout the interview.

a2-09.q: Mrs. Ortega tells Daniela: 'El puesto es suyo.' What does suyo mean here?
a2-09.why: With usted, the possessive is suyo/suya: el puesto es suyo = the job is yours. Context shows she is talking to Daniela.

a2-09.q: Fill in the blank: Mrs. Ortega asks Daniela (usted): ¿Ha ___ antes con clientes?
a2-09.why: Present perfect = haber + participle (-ado/-ido); with usted, haber is ha. The participle doesn't change for gender (not trabajada), trabajando is the gerund, and trabajo is the present.

a2-09.q: What is the difference between 'Daniela se despertó' and 'Daniela despertó a su hermana'?
options: Both mean that Daniela woke up.
The first: she woke up; the second: she woke her sister up.
The first: she woke her sister up; the second: she woke up.
The first is present, the second is past.
a2-09.why: With se the action falls back on the subject: se despertó = she woke up. Without se the verb takes an object: despertó a su hermana = she woke her sister up. Both are preterite.

a2-09.q: The older woman asks with tú: '¿Sabes dónde está la oficina?' How would she ask with usted?
a2-09.why: Usted uses the he/she form: (usted) sabe. Sabes is the tú form, and sabéis is vosotros (plural, Spain).

a2-09.q: Fill in the blank: La señora mayor entró en la sala y ___ junto a la jefa.
a2-09.why: Sentarse (to sit down) is reflexive, and the story tells finished events in the preterite: se sentó.

a2-10.q: Which sentence means 'It's the biggest lantern in the village'?
options: Es el farol más grande que el pueblo.
Es farol el más grande en pueblo.
Es el farol más grande del pueblo.
Es el farol grande más del pueblo.
a2-10.why: The superlative is el + noun + más + adjective + de (del = de + el), where English uses 'in'.

a2-10.topic: Perfect tenses: he visto, había aprendido
a2-10.q: Fill in the blank: Cuando Dolores llegó al granero, la lluvia ya ___ el papel.
a2-10.why: The rain soaked the paper before another past moment (when Dolores arrived), so use the past perfect: había + participle. Ha mojado connects to now, not to a past moment.

a2-10.q: Fill in the blank (that year): ___ año, Dolores tenía una misión especial.
a2-10.why: Año is masculine, so 'that' is ese. Esa and esta are feminine, and esto is neuter (not used before a noun).

a2-10.q: Why does the story say 'aquella fue la mejor noche de su vida'?
options: Aquella is for things close to the speaker.
Aquella points to a night far back in time.
a2-10.why: Aquel/aquella = that (far away), often for a moment in the distant past. Este/esta is for near things or now.

a2-10.q: Fill in the blanks: Después de la lluvia, el toro era ___ bonito ___ antes.
a2-10.why: To compare two things: más + adjective + que. Más de is used before numbers (más de cien personas), and tan pairs with como.

a2-10.topic: Perfect tenses: he visto, había aprendido
options: Nunca he veído trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
Nunca visto he trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
Nunca he visto trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
Nunca he vista trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
a2-10.why: Ver has an irregular participle, visto, which never changes for gender; he and the participle always stay together.
Demonstratives agree with the noun: este pueblo (m.), esta vez (f.), aquella noche (f.).

a2-10.q: Fill in the blank: Es la fiesta más importante ___ pueblo.
a2-10.why: In superlatives Spanish uses de where English says 'in': la fiesta más importante del pueblo.
